title: IMAGO VITAE
subtitle: The Will He Could Not Write
credits: One synthetic rehearsal voice with one original ambient score. Opening is an explicitly credited editorial rendering of Tacitus, Annals 15.62. The remainder is selected and abridged editorial English renderings of Seneca, Epistulae Morales 26.1–10 with exact Latin excerpts. The letter predates his death and is not Seneca’s written will or last spoken words.
disclaimer: This is a curated reading, NOT the last letter of Seneca and not a surviving will. The narration is synthetic and preliminary.

cues.speaker: NARRATOR
cues.text: Tacitus reports that Seneca asked for the writing tablets of his will.
cues.latin: Ille interritus poscit testamenti tabulas.
cues.source: Tacitus, Annals 15.62; editorial paraphrase, not an exact quotation

cues.speaker: NARRATOR
cues.text: The centurion refused. He left his friends only what remained: the image of his life.
cues.latin: ac denegante centurione ... imaginem vitae suae relinquere testatur
cues.source: Tacitus, Annals 15.62; editorial paraphrase, not an exact quotation

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I told you I was within sight of old age. Now I fear that old age is already behind me.
cues.latin: Modo dicebam tibi in conspectu esse me senectutis: iam vereor ne senectutem post me reliquerim.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.1; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Years have marked my body. Yet I do not feel their injury in my mind.
cues.latin: non sentio in animo aetatis iniuriam, cum sentiam in corpore.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.2; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Each day takes something away from our strength.
cues.latin: carpimur, singuli dies aliquid subtrahunt viribus.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.4; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Is there a better end than slowly to dissolve, as nature releases us?
cues.latin: ecquis exitus est melior quam in finem suum natura solvente dilabi?
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.4; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I watch myself, as though the day has come which must judge all the years of my life.
cues.latin: ego certe, velut appropinquet experimentum et ille laturus sententiam de omnibus annis meis dies venerit, ita me observo et alloquor:
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.4; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I will entrust to death the measure of my progress.
cues.latin: quid profecerim morti crediturus sum.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.5; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: That day will reveal whether I only speak with courage, or truly feel it.
cues.latin: utrum loquar fortia an sentiam
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.5; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Put aside the opinions of other people. They are always uncertain.
cues.latin: Remove existimationem hominum: dubia semper est et in partem utramque dividitur.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Put aside the studies pursued throughout your life. Death will pronounce the judgment.
cues.latin: Remove studia tota vita tractata: mors de te pronuntiatura est.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Learned conversation and the sayings of wise men do not reveal the true strength of the soul.
cues.latin: disputationes et litterata colloquia et ex praeceptis sapientium verba collecta et eruditus sermo non ostendunt verum robur animi
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Even a frightened man may speak bravely.
cues.latin: est enim oratio etiam timidissimis audax.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: What you have done will be clear when you draw your last breath.
cues.latin: Quid egeris tunc apparebit cum animam ages.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Accipio condicionem. Non reformido iudicium.
cues.latin: Accipio condicionem, non reformido iudicium.
cues.translation: I accept the condition. I do not fear the judgment.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6; exact Latin, punctuation normalized

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I say these things to myself. But take them as spoken to you as well.
cues.latin: Haec mecum loquor, sed tecum quoque me locutum puta.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.7; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: You are younger. What difference does it make? Years are not counted.
cues.latin: Iuvenior es: quid refert? non dinumerantur anni.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.7; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Incertum est quo loco te mors exspectet. Itaque tu illam omni loco exspecta.
cues.latin: Incertum est quo loco te mors exspectet; itaque tu illam omni loco exspecta.
cues.translation: You cannot know where death awaits you; therefore be ready for it everywhere.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.7; exact Latin, punctuation normalized

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: To meditate on death is to meditate on freedom.
cues.latin: Meditare mortem: qui hoc dicit meditari libertatem iubet.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.10; English rendering of his reflection on an Epicurean maxim quoted in 26.8

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Whoever has learned how to die has unlearned how to be a slave.
cues.latin: Qui mori didicit servire dedidicit.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.10; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: There is only one chain that binds us: the love of life.
cues.latin: Una est catena quae nos alligatos tenet, amor vitae.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.10; original editorial English rendering

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: We need not cast it away. Only loosen its hold, so that when necessity comes, we are ready.
cues.latin: qui ut non est abiciendus, ita minuendus est, ut si quando res exiget ... parati simus
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.10; original editorial English rendering, abridged

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Vale.
cues.latin: Vale.
cues.source: Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.10; exact Latin closing
